name: Far left
summary: Far-left politics is a family of ideologies, chiefly communism and anarchism, that seek to abolish capitalism and private ownership of the means of production in favour of a classless society with collective ownership and distribution by need. It is internationalist, egalitarian and revolutionary in aim, though strands diverge sharply on the state, party leadership, violence and democracy.
scope: Profile of the shared core of the revolutionary anti-capitalist left as documented on Wikipedia and in the Communist Manifesto and the Stanford Encyclopedia entries on Marx and anarchism. Where Marxist-Leninists and anarchists differ (state, planning, vanguard parties, dictatorship of the proletariat) the answer is 0. It excludes social democracy and the far-right-aligned readings of communist states.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Collective provision of basic needs fits the far left's aim of going beyond social democracy, and the Manifesto already lists free public education.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Reforms are accepted only as temporary steps, so a wage rise is supported but not central; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The far left opposes capitalism and neoliberalism and seeks a post-capitalist economy.

public-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership of the means of production is central, though anarchists want common rather than state ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto proposes a heavy progressive income tax; anarchists prefer expropriation to taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are valued as organs of worker power, notably in anarcho-syndicalism, though often seen as insufficient alone.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto's central demand is abolishing bourgeois private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is a stopgap short of abolishing capitalist ownership; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: The far left rejects neoliberalism and treats social reforms as steps to defend, not cut.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership by the producers is the core economic aim.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anarchist and left critiques of coercive state power make security surveillance suspect; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: New Left and anarchist currents favour personal freedom from state prohibition; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anarchists distrust state censorship while many other leftists back restricting fascist speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy and Marxists place power in the working class, not a leader; Leninist vanguards complicate this.

state-harmful.rationale: Anarchists reject the state outright while Marxists expect a transitional state that withers away.

limit-guns.rationale: Adherents are split, as many favour arming workers while others back controls; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: If the state is an instrument of class rule, strengthening its coercive arms is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: New Left currents favour decriminalisation, but views on sex work are divided; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Anarchists favour decentralised communes while Marxist-Leninists favour centralisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Kropotkin called prisons schools for crime, and the left generally favours reform over punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto expects the bourgeois family to vanish with capital.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The New Left championed gay rights, though anarchists are often indifferent to state marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: The New Left and feminist currents backed abortion rights.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is treated as an illusion of alienated conditions; liberation theology is a minority exception.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: New Left currents made racial justice a core cause.

gender-social-construct.rationale: New Left feminist currents lean this way; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and national divisions are fading.

gradual-change.rationale: The aim is a radical rupture with property relations, with reforms only as steps.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The far left is internationalist and anarchists question borders.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposition to globalisation and the EU suggests distrust of existing international bodies; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Internationalism is a founding principle, though Stalinism tied it to the USSR.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Suspicion of Western power makes endorsement unlikely; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Cosmopolitan anarchists and Marxist internationalists look past borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Scholars dispute whether Marx was productivist or proto-degrowth, and adherents split likewise.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Since the 1960s the far left has backed radical, rapid climate action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Marx is read as productivist but technology is seen as shaped by class relations; split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Many far-left groups opposed nuclear power in the 1980s.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution is the defining method, though some groups now work within systems.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anarchists and councilists reject rule by specialists; Leninist vanguards complicate this; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Marxist-Leninists favour planned economies while anarchists reject central direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mutualists accept markets among worker-owned firms; most Marxists and communists do not.

land-value-tax.rationale: The Manifesto seeks abolition of land ownership rather than a single tax; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: Views are divided between support as a reform and rejection as sustaining wage labor; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Internationalism cuts against tariffs while anti-globalisation cuts for them; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Marxist currents want state direction while anarchists reject it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The aim is collective, not small-owner, property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Manifesto treats wage labor as capital's basis and communism ends it; Kropotkin's anarcho-communism shares this.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Marx proposed centralising credit in the state while anarcho-communists abolish money; split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class collaboration through state bodies is opposed in favour of class struggle.

one-party-rule.rationale: Leninist currents defend vanguard parties while anarchists and many others reject them.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Republicanism is part of far-left history and hereditary rule is opposed.

democracy-best.rationale: The far left generally opposes liberal democracy but favours direct or participatory forms.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct and participatory democracy are favoured over representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Council-style rule echoes the Paris Commune and anarcho-syndicalism, though Leninists often subordinate them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Positions range from anarchist decentralism to centralist communist states; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Opposition to unjustified hierarchy is the core of anarchism and of class-free communism.

political-violence-never.rationale: Violence is held justified against capitalist repression by some groups, though others are pacifist.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is seen as an instrument of ruling classes; inferred from internationalism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is a private matter and an illusion to fade, so state religion is opposed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is seen as ideology of alienation; scripture-based law is opposed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatising coercive functions serves property owners and is opposed (anarcho-capitalism is rejected by the far left).

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Manifesto holds national divisions are fading and class is the basis of unity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens by calling history the history of class struggles.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The far left favours equality of outcome over equal opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anarchist and decolonial currents back this; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Class internationalism, not civilisational blocs, is the organising principle; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Solidarity and collective ownership are central, and individual accumulation is condemned.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Marx criticised liberal rights as separating people, but anarchists stress autonomy; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Green anarchism says yes; Marxists often treat nature instrumentally.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists historically reject Malthusian framing; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-primitivism is a minor variant; most of the far left seeks to take over industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Productivist and eco-critical readings of Marx diverge; split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anarchist and democratic emphasis on direct control; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Distrust of state surveillance suggests support; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Manifesto seeks revolutionary change, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Far-left politics is strongly ideological; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Anarchists favour direct action while Marxist strands also use parties and elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative anarchists insist on it while Leninists accept a dictatorial transition.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Anarcho-primitivism is only one minor variant.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Communism is described as ending systematic alienation; the specific claim is inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is a defining far-left aim, and Kropotkin's motto was all for all.

production-for-use.rationale: Production to expand capital is the Manifesto's target.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit is surplus value drawn from workers' labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marxist-Leninists affirm it, anarchists reject any post-revolutionary state.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto proposes public farmland and anarchists favour collectives; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: This is the Leninist line; inferred for the wider family.

taxation-theft.rationale: Marxists back taxation and anarchists oppose the state; the 'theft' framing is rare on the left.

harm-principle.rationale: Anarchists partly accept it but Marxists reject liberal individualism; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Marx critiqued liberal rights as rights of separation and the left stresses class and collective claims.

conscription.rationale: Anarchists oppose it and others split; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Collective political voice is prized; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Human emancipation requires material conditions beyond formal rights.

media-academia-power.rationale: The left locates power in capital and ruling-class control of media rather than in academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from class analysis and New Left antiracism.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporate representation blurs class struggle; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Anarchists reject it and others expect the state to wither, though Stalinist states approached it.

national-rebirth.rationale: Class, not national decadence, is the frame.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Opposition to hierarchy and feudal relations.

bound-labor.rationale: The far left opposes bound and exploited labor.

universal-morality.rationale: Marx saw morality as historically conditioned and was wary of universal claims.

single-common-good.rationale: Politics is analysed as class conflict until classes disappear; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Internationalist and anti-colonial currents are suspicious; Soviet-era positions varied.

revive-national-language.rationale: Mixed attitudes to national projects; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic worker control follows from collective ownership.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Manifesto calls for free public education.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom in the market sense is rejected; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Anarchists value moral example but Marxists hold that material conditions decide; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Support for some national movements coexists with internationalism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religion is treated as illusion and a materialist critique is favoured.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalism rejects dividing workers by nationality.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Opposition to neoliberal conditionality; the Manifesto's universal work obligation complicates this.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class antagonism is the Manifesto's starting point.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist currents back common fronts; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers have no country and should unite internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: New Left currents championed women's equality.

ban-interest.rationale: Marx proposed state control of credit but there is no settled ban; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposed by the far left in all strands.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marx's models vary, but the state serving the ruling class is the standard far-left reading.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Pro-environment currents favour radical climate action.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Internationalism and opposition to national culture as a bar.

elite-replacement.rationale: Rejected conspiracy framing; the far left stresses class, inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Mixed views on parliamentary forms; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: New Left currents criticise male privilege as systemic.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Elites serve ruling-class interests; the corruption framing is inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Opposition to state coercion suggests support; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto proposes extensive state economic measures and ends property rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality is central though liberal rights language is criticised.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stalinism affirmed it, Trotskyists and left communists denied it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial currents lean this way; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: equality before one law fits the far left, though anarchists reject state law altogether.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: the far left opposes religious coercion but also state policing of belief.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: a secular, materialist tradition does not legislate religious taboos.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Manifesto demands free public education, and the secular Marxist and anarchist traditions oppose church instruction in it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Split: Marxist-Leninists strengthen the state under threat, anarchists reject it outright.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Anarchists hold authority needs free consent and Marxists ground rule in class, so adherents split with a lean to agree.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Manifesto says the ruling ideas of each age are those of the ruling class, and the SEP entry on Marx covers ideology as serving class interest.

trade-surplus.rationale: The far left is internationalist and rejects national economic rivalry; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Internationalism and 'working men have no country' make expelling minorities incompatible with the core far-left view.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Manifesto calls for forcible overthrow and abolition of private property, so force to reach the goal is accepted.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Anarchists and communists stress mutual aid and cooperation and reject capitalist competition as the driver of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Marxist-Leninists accept banning opponents while anarchists oppose any state power to ban parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The SEP entry on anarchism centers domination and hierarchy, and Marxists treat wage labor as dependence on capital.

separated-powers.rationale: Anarchists favor decentralized checks, while Marxist-Leninist strands concentrate power in the party-state.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninists demand a vanguard party; anarchists and council communists reject it.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Manifesto frames communism as the movement of the immense majority in the interest of the poorest class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Selling off public housing into private ownership cuts against collective ownership, though some strands accept tenant ownership; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Manifesto treats labour's organisation and class struggle as central, so legal limits on strikes are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marx's critique of political economy traces poverty to exploitation and property relations, not to population pressure.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The far left is internationalist and holds that class, not ethnicity, divides societies; the Manifesto says workers have no country.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Anarchists and some libertarian socialists favour sortition while Marxist-Leninists favour party leadership; strands split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Marxist-Leninists accept the dictatorship of the proletariat while anarchists reject emergency state powers; strands split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from distribution by need and Marx's hostility to profiteering; controls are accepted as a stopgap.

party-controls-media.rationale: Marxist-Leninist states have run party-controlled media while anarchists oppose any state control; strands split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Marxist-Leninists place the army under party command, anarchists reject standing armies altogether; strands split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and 'workers have no country'; far-left movements generally back open borders.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Commune model of officials on a workman's wage is the shared reference of the Marxist and anarchist left, against privileged office-holders.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Marxist-Leninists demand binding democratic centralism while anarchists reject party command and hierarchy, so the family is split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: the far left is internationalist but generally treats the EU as a capitalist bloc rather than a form of pooled sovereignty it wants.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people, and anarchists reject the executive state entirely.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: the far left opposes state churches and hierarchical religious authority, though the issue is peripheral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Marx treated religion as a reflection of alienation and anarchists oppose all authority, so clerical rule is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country, and the Marxist and anarchist left oppose inter-imperialist wars as a ruling-class affair.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred: anarchists reject censorship and the Marxist tradition is divided (Soviet state control of culture), so a mild disagreement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist states have often removed limits while anarchists reject presidents, so the family is split.

recall-officials.rationale: The Commune principle of revocable delegates is held by both Marxists and anarchists.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Internationalist and anti-imperialist, the far left opposes military blocs and overseas bases; inferred from this rather than a stated programme.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Far-left strands want landlordism ended through collective or public ownership, not universal private home ownership, which Engels criticised; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Marx praised the Commune for replacing the standing army with the armed people, and anarchists favour popular militias, though Marxist-Leninist states kept regular armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto calls for blurring the town-country divide through industry and dismisses rural life as a refuge of virtue; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Internationalism ('workers have no country') discounts nation-state borders, yet anti-colonial left movements backed reunification; adherents are split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The left champions education for all and sees intellectuals as able to join the proletariat, so it does not treat schooling as alienating; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-colonial and internationalist egalitarianism rejects ranking peoples, though Marx's stage theory of history is sometimes read otherwise; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state's power to kill while Marxist-Leninist states used capital punishment, so strands diverge.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Manifesto demands free public education and the end of bourgeois family hierarchies, which fits teaching about sex and gender equality; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marx's materialism treats religion as ideology and the far left favours secular scientific schooling.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Anti-pornography feminists on the left and anarchists opposed to state censorship disagree, so no common line.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Internationalism rejects defining membership by ancestry or nation; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Support for national minorities and equal rights extends to languages in public life, though it is not a core demand; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Equal application of law and hostility to religion as ideology cut against special exemptions, though the left backs minority rights; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Manifesto looks to a society where the free development of each is the condition of all, and anarchists prize individuality; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and internationalism; cancellation of poor-country debt is a common far-left demand but not in the core sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Far-left strands hold that national independence leaves class rule intact, though anarchists reject nation-state independence as a goal; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Marxist-Leninists favour councils or party constitution making while anarchists reject constitutions, so adherents are split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Marxist-Leninists accepted such restrictions in the name of development, while anarchists and left communists reject them; split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Internationalism implies solidarity with the world's poor, though the far left stresses redistribution by revolution rather than charity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: the far left opposes national arsenals and capitalist militarism, though states ruled by Marxist-Leninists built them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and Marxists favour delegates revocable by councils over strong presidencies.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Manifesto calls for a state bank centralising credit under public control, and anarchists oppose central banks altogether; both reject independence from the people.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Internationalism and rejection of nationalism mean historic-homeland claims carry little weight; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing bourgeois property in the interest of the whole community, so private ownership is subordinate to the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Left communists and anarchists call the USSR state capitalist while Marxist-Leninists call it socialist, so adherents split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: the far left backs collective control of production, which makes precaution against ecological harm natural, but this is not a core text.

collective-defense.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country, and the far left generally opposes military alliances as instruments of states and capital.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Marxists favour subordinating the church and abolishing religion, but anarchists oppose state control of anything; strands split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the Commune model of delegates under popular control, which has no place for an office above class.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Marxist-Leninists accept force to preserve a socialist state while anarchists reject it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from federalist and autonomy proposals in the anarchist tradition.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Marx treats religion and divine authority as ideology that supports ruling classes; anarchists reject all rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive or graduated income tax among its measures.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marx holds that social circumstances shape people and that changed conditions change character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers entirely and the Commune model makes officials accountable and recallable.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The far left rejects rule by a few over the many; the Commune and anarchist models give power to the people.

leader-cult.rationale: Anarchists and many Marxists reject hierarchy and personality cults, though some Marxist-Leninist states practised them.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist and anarchist traditions expect a new bureaucratic class to arise after revolution and require continuing struggle against it.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing property in land and applying rents to public purposes, and the left generally backs land reform.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and solidarity with the displaced.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country, and the left rejects nationality-based territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Marxist critique of religion and the anarchist defence of liberty both oppose penalties for leaving a faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian and anti-authoritarian principles opposing legal compulsion over dress.

common-currency.rationale: No shared position; adherents range from anti-capitalist critics of the euro to internationalists.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Manifesto's internationalism unites workers by class, not by ancestry or language.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Split between Austromarxist cultural autonomy and Leninist or anarchist rejection of national structures.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and class solidarity: equal rights where people live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marx's materialist conception of history makes the mode of production the base, though anarchists give ideas more weight.

ban-cartels.rationale: The left seeks to abolish concentrated private capital, not to preserve competitive markets.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: the left objects to spending public money to rescue capital owners.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Paris Commune model has elected, recallable judges and officials answerable to the majority, though anarchists distrust majority rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian left's general support for gender equality measures.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Manifesto's world-market internationalism opposes national seclusion, though some strands favour socialist autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: the left backs workers' rights and environmental limits on trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Communism's 'from each according to ability' and the call to end wage labour imply social duty over private gain, though strands differ.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Split: Leninists and guerrilla currents favour vanguards, while Marx and many anarchists say conditions must mature.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of all rights of inheritance, and the left rejects birth privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Internationalist and class-based, the far left rejects nation-centred history, though it has no single curriculum doctrine; inferred from the internationalism in s1 and s2.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Communist Manifesto and the anti-imperialist tradition reject rule of one people by another, whatever the stated aim.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Manifesto holds workers have no country and the far left is internationalist, so it distrusts schooling in national pride; Marxist-Leninist states are the exception.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Most of the far left backs measures against racial disadvantage, though some strands prefer class-based remedies; inferred from its egalitarianism.

public-money-creation.rationale: Collective control of credit is in the Manifesto's programme (a national bank with state capital); anarchists would reject a state issuer, so the answer is mild.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marx held that capitalism's contradictions produce recurring crises that end in its overthrow, and the far left treats collapse as the basis of its aim.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The far left is anti-imperialist and internationalist, so it rejects claims to influence based on past empire; inferred, as Soviet practice differed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strands favour delinking, while orthodox Marxists see world integration as progressive and anarchists vary; adherents are split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin's labor-aristocracy thesis is held by Marxist-Leninists, but the Manifesto and anarchists hold that workers everywhere share a common class interest.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The far left is egalitarian and opposes discrimination, and rejects property rights as grounds for exclusion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Marx saw bourgeois rights as protecting property and the Commune model favoured recallable, accountable delegates over entrenched limits; anarchists reject constitutions.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Paris Commune, a model for the far left, had elected, recallable officials; anarchists likewise reject hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Anarchists favor consent and Marxist-Leninists favor democratic centralism binding the minority, so the answer is split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the revolutionary tradition; not tied to constitutional law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Commune is praised as a working body replacing parliamentarism; anarchists reject parliaments too.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Some anarchist strands stress animal liberation; inferred as a mild majority.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Manifesto rejects the privileged class's charity and aims to abolish class.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Manifesto calls for workers to take political power and revolution is the central task.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view that the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view that ruling-class ideas dominate; hegemony is a later extension.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Manifesto describes the bourgeoisie exploiting the world market; far-left anti-imperialism extends this.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Manifesto states workers have no country and calls for international unity.

party-own-road.rationale: Marxist-Leninists historically accepted central direction while anarchists reject any party; split.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and rejection of national autarky.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Manifesto expects national divisions to vanish; border claims are not a far-left aim.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the far left stresses class, not descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from far-left opposition to fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Marxist-Leninists reject the equivalence outright and anarchists condemn both unevenly; inferred majority view.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: Marx backed the Union and saw slavery as central; the question is not directly sourced.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the far left's critical view of honors to oppressors.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the class and patriarchy analysis that stresses women's victimization.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's universal, internationalist claims.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Commune abolished the standing army and replaced it with the armed people; anarchists reject armies.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the aim of collective provision and equality; adherents differ on paying wages.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto attacks the bourgeois family and anarchists reject inherited authority, though practice varied.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Paris Commune model, praised by Marx, made all officials elected and recallable rather than appointed by examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Adherents split: anti-imperialists favour national control, but internationalists reject nationalist economic barriers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto critique of the bourgeois family and the left tradition of freeing marriage from property and church.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Commune made delegates instructed and revocable at any time; anarchists likewise reject independent representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: private capital-market accounts contradict the aim of collective provision by need.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing property in land, and the anarchist tradition holds land by occupancy and use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Adherents split: Marxist-Leninists use legislatures tactically, anarchists and council communists reject bourgeois parliaments.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from internationalism, which opposes imposing one national language, though some Marxist-Leninist states did.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from internationalism, which rejects nationalist restrictions on who may hold land, and from collective land ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the far left framing of inequality as structural rather than a matter of individual intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist critique of commodity culture and waste.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Adherents split: Leninists back national liberation movements, anarchists oppose funding by states.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: anarchists and council communists oppose it, while Marxist-Leninists split over Soviet interventions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Capitalist influence over the state is the far left's core claim; the Manifesto calls the modern state the committee managing the bourgeoisie's affairs.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: the far left is internationalist and anti-imperialist, so it distrusts sovereignty-based controls, though it opposes foreign capital's influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the far left does not treat population growth as a state aim and favours universal provision over natalist incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: anti-speculation and anti-gentrification sentiment pulls one way, internationalism and open movement the other.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Manifesto's programme includes equal obligation of all to labour, which fits a guaranteed right to work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Leninist and anarchist critiques of imperialism treat liberal democracies as capitalist states that wage wars abroad.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: anarchists reject any duty to obey the state outright, while Marxists see law as an instrument of class rule; adherents lean to agree.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: revolutionary internationalism supports solidarity with insurgent workers across borders, against the 'for any reason' absolute.

industrial-unions.rationale: Syndicalist and Marxist traditions organise workers as a class across crafts, with industrial unionism as the typical anarcho-syndicalist form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: class internationalism and egalitarianism reject blaming an ethnic or religious minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolition of the bourgeois family, and anarchists reject state-sanctioned marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: the Paris Commune model stressed accountable, transparent officials.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: anarchist and eco-left strands favour local self-sufficiency, but Marxist strands favour large-scale planned production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchists favour affinity groups while Marxist-Leninists favour permanent parties under democratic centralism, so adherents are split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: internationalism subordinates national constitutions to class solidarity, though the far left rejects liberal international institutions too.

religious-nation.rationale: The Manifesto and the anarchist tradition are hostile to religion and hold that workers have no country.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Internationalism and anti-imperialism reject tributary submission to a dominant state; the Manifesto calls for ending the exploitation of one nation by another.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from internationalist redistribution by need across all people; regional hoarding of revenue cuts against solidarity.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto distinguishes abolishing bourgeois property in the means of production from personal possessions, which stay.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism is the far left's own aim, so adherents reject defeating it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from collective ownership aims; adherents favour public provision over private and market providers inside the system.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx called religion the opium of the people, an illusion consoling real suffering, though anarchists and others vary on how it fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Manifesto credits the bourgeoisie with unprecedented productive forces that create the material basis for socialism, while still demanding its abolition.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto ties the position of women to the bourgeois family and property relations, and the left holds equality requires ending the economic order.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto calls for replacing domestic education and the bourgeois family order; socialising housework and childcare is a long-standing left demand, though not all strands stress it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; the left rejects linguistic nationalism and purism as nationalist reaction.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred; sympathy for indigenous and national self-determination competes with anarchist and Marxist doubt that state treaties bind anyone.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Anarchist and communalist strands favour federations of self-governing communities holding property in common, while Marxist-Leninists favour a state-planned order; adherents are split but lean agree.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to national oppression; state-encouraged settlement of a dominant group is rejected.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Far-left adherents hold that communism or anarchist socialism is the sound basis for society, rejecting a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and the far left is internationalist, so historical or religious ties to land confer no special claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Far-left tradition opposes antisemitism and the far right that denies the Holocaust; denial is incompatible with the internationalist, egalitarian core.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anarchists and communists campaign for sexual freedom and oppose state regulation of private life, though some Marxist-Leninist states criminalised homosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Marxist-Leninists accept suppressing counter-revolutionary opposition during the transition while anarchists reject it; the strands split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology and the far left opposes state coercion of belief, including blasphemy law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Manifesto and Marx oppose exploitation; the far left is anti-imperialist and rejects governing territories for a ruling country's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The far left supports anti-imperialist resistance but does not frame it as a religious duty; not addressed in the sources.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The far left is secular; Marx treats religion as ideology and so rejects removing rulers for not governing by religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Paris Commune text calls for revocable delegates and workers' self-government, and anarchism favours direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Marxist class analysis combined with anarchist and later far-left work on race and gender supports overlapping oppressions, though orthodox Marxists put class first.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from far-left support for liberation movements; early Marxist-Leninist states differed.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue; the far left is split between supporters and sceptics of how it would operate under capitalism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Far-left thought holds that class division is the core of politics and does not seek to combine left and right ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's theory of alienation holds that wage labour estranges workers from their product and activity.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The internationalist and secular far left rejects civilisational essentialism about Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marx and the far left reject divine authority and ground authority in the people or the working class.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The far left is secular and favours keeping religion out of the state, though some adherents defend personal religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the far left's support for workers' rights against employers; not addressed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: The far left aims to replace the market economy rather than combine it with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Commune text replaces the standing army with the armed people, and anarchists oppose armies; Marxist-Leninists accept armed forces in the transition.

rich-first.rationale: Egalitarian and internationalist principles reject letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The far left is anti-militarist and opposes imperialist blocs; some Marxist-Leninists aligned with the Soviet bloc.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession contradicts the egalitarian, anti-hierarchical core of communism and anarchism, which reject inherited privilege.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not a defining issue; cooperative, user-owned finance fits the far left's collective ownership aim, but Marxists want banks nationalised and anarchists differ.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from far-left internationalism and anti-imperialism, which oppose creditor-imposed austerity; the sources do not discuss the IMF.

property-franchise.rationale: The Communist Manifesto attacks property-based class rule and the far left seeks to abolish bourgeois privilege, so a property franchise is rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecosocialist and social-ecology currents link the two, but orthodox Marxists do not stress it; inferred from anarchist and Marxist critiques of domination.

reification.rationale: Marx's analysis of commodity fetishism, the basis of the Marxist current, holds that capitalism makes social relations appear as relations between things.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The far left holds that bourgeois freedoms are formal while capital owns the press; the Manifesto treats bourgeois freedom as that of the owners.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers entirely and Marxists treat law as class instrument; the statement's legalism is inferred as mildly disagreeable.

racial-franchise.rationale: The far left is internationalist and egalitarian, and rejects any racial or ethnic limit on political rights.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from far-left support for direct participation, as in the Paris Commune; the sources predate the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the Commune model of accountable, transparent officials; the sources do not discuss open data.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The far left treats religion as a private matter and opposes legal restrictions on marriage on religious grounds.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The far left is internationalist and opposes sectarian and ethnic division of workers.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the Commune-style direct, recallable popular rule the far left favours and anarchist anti-representative thinking; sortition is not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marxist hostility to religion and religious-socialist currents pull apart, and the sources do not address reinterpreting doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The far left holds that private ownership of the means of production gives owners power over workers and the state, which the Manifesto sets out.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the far left's opposition to oppression and hierarchy; practice varied across historical regimes.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marxist-Leninists favour anti-religious education while anarchists oppose state-run belief policy, so adherents split.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Anarchists want policing and prisons abolished while Marxist-Leninists keep state coercion in the transition, so adherents split.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on class over communal identity and on majority working-class democracy.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the aim of collective provision and mutual aid rather than philanthropy that leaves the system intact.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the Commune model of revocable delegates paid workmen's wages, which limits office as a career.

vote-delegation.rationale: Revocable delegates are central to the Commune model and anarchist federalism; subject-by-subject delegation is an inference.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and adherents differ on how far to prioritise it over class struggle.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the far left's opposition to hierarchy and gender oppression.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Manifesto attacks the bourgeois family and subordination of women; inferred that spousal equality follows.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's internationalism (workers have no country); the far left rejects citizenship as a basis for excluding residents from political life.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the far left's aim of decommodifying basic needs; rent caps are a common interim demand though not a goal in themselves.

abolish-ip.rationale: Marxists and anarchists both oppose private appropriation of ideas, but Marxist-Leninist states kept state-run copyright, so strands split; inferred from the property critique.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and anti-militarism: drilled youth organised for national service serves the nation rather than the class, though Marxist-Leninist states ran pioneer movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the far left's anti-militarist and internationalist stance against nuclear arms as instruments of states.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism, which treats foreign bases as tools of imperial power.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the far left's solidarity with victims of colonial and state violence; not a doctrinal point.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto's core claim is that wage labour is exploited by capital and that bourgeois property should be abolished, so income should flow from work, not ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Marxists endorse revolutionary and defensive violence and most anarchists accept self-defence, though a pacifist minority exists; inferred from the sources' treatment of revolution.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Manifesto treats national differences as fading and class as the main division; inferred, as the question of national continuity is not addressed directly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Feminist and queer-influenced currents on the left accept it while orthodox Marxists emphasise material conditions; adherents are split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Adherents split between class-first Marxists and identity-aware currents; the sources do not address it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from internationalism: honouring those who die for the nation as saints conflicts with class loyalty, though revolutionary martyrs are honoured.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marx's materialist view treats politics as class struggle grounded in economic conditions and religion as ideology, not as a struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Manifesto is internationalist and does not discuss diaspora homelands; inferred indifference.

culture-before-state.rationale: Marxist base-superstructure thinking puts changing material and class relations before cultural renewal; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Mostly secular, so the question seldom arises; the Christian-anarchist and liberation-theology wing would agree, so no clear line.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Adherents are mostly secular and uninterested, while religious socialists would agree; no common line.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Internationalism and class equality oppose giving economic life to an ethnic or national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Marxists and anarchists differ on self-determination and territorial units versus federations; the sources do not settle it.

independent-unions.rationale: Anarchists and syndicalists insist on independent unions while Marxist-Leninists accept party-led unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Manifesto makes the proletariat's winning of political power the means to socialism, though Marxist-Leninists accept party rule on its behalf.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Collective ownership of the means of production and distribution by need implies public control of basic services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Commune model of a single working body and anarchist rejection of institutional checks; weakly sourced.

municipal-property.rationale: Anarchist and communalist strands accept local ownership while Marxists favour social or state ownership, so the answer is split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Anarchists favour federations of delegates with no governing power, while Marxist-Leninists use democratic centralism; split.

family-wage.rationale: The far left aims at distribution by need, not a wage tied to a worker's family, and it has no shared view on it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the far-left sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anarchists lean yes and Marxist-Leninists favour state control of finance, so adherents split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anarchists favour it while authoritarian communist strands do not; adherents split.

person-over-state.rationale: Anarchists put the individual first, while Marxist-Leninists subordinate the individual to class and party; split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marxist materialism and most anarchist secularism reject it, though religious anarchist strands exist; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Anarchists reject national authority and Marxist-Leninists favour centralism; split.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between technological optimism and green anarchist opposition.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the far-left sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The far left stresses class and internationalism over race, as the Manifesto's appeal to workers of all countries suggests, though anti-racist self-organisation is common; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and rejection of racial hierarchy; some adherents back pride among oppressed groups.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anti-militarist anarchists lean yes while revolutionary communists support wars of liberation; split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The far left is internationalist and sees nations as bourgeois constructs; the Manifesto says the workers have no country.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the aim of class unity: separate religious electorates divide workers and are rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the far left explains conflict through capital and imperialism rather than plots against a national homeland, and is internationalist.

free-public-college.rationale: The Manifesto demands free education for all children in public schools, and the far left generally extends this to higher education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: eco-socialist and anarchist strands prefer abolishing capitalist production or direct regulation over market-style taxes, so adherents split.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: not a defining demand, but eco-socialist and anarchist strands stress ecological stewardship against capitalist exploitation.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: class analysis treats gender equality as material, and most far-left strands reject essentialist claims about women's values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: anarchist and pacifist strands favour disarmament, while Marxist-Leninists support armed defence of revolutionary states.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: the far left opposes secret deals between bourgeois governments, but the documented sources do not discuss diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto's call to centralise credit in the state implies control of capital, but anarchists reject state controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Commune model replaces the standing army with the armed people and anarchists reject state monopoly on force, though Marxist-Leninists favour a worker state's armed force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Manifesto and Marx's internationalism treat inter-state wars as bourgeois affairs, and anarchists urge refusal, though both back revolutionary war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Marx and anarchists value union organisation as class struggle, though they see bargaining as a step, not the goal.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the far left seeks to abolish wage labour rather than top up its pay within capitalism.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from rejection of capitalist limits on public spending; adherents who abolish the state do not set borrowing rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Internationalist anti-imperialism fits the aim, but the far left seeks to end capitalism rather than restructure its rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anarchists and the Commune model smash the state, while Marxist-Leninists use a transitional workers' state, so adherents split as the scope says.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Anarchists favour open experiments without a blueprint while Marxist-Leninists favour central planning, so the family splits.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the far left rejects pricing nature as capital as further commodification under private ownership.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto states that workers have no country and the far left is internationalist.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from egalitarianism and opposition to debt as a tool of exploitation; the sources do not discuss it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Marxist and anarchist currents apply the idea unevenly, and the sources do not discuss it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marx saw human nature as historically formed while some anarchists hold a cooperative nature, so the family splits.

public-service-media.rationale: Anarchists reject state-funded media while Marxist-Leninists favour state-run media, and the sources do not address it.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism should be replaced by a different economic system rather than reformed.
missingStatements.rationale: Abolishing capitalism rather than reforming it is the defining aim of the far left.
missingStatements.declined: Already captured by markets-allocate-better, public-ownership, worker-ownership, production-for-use and gradual-change; a further statement would not separate the far left from other socialisms.

notes: Heterogeneous umbrella: Marxist-Leninist, anarchist, left-communist and New Left strands differ on the state, vanguard parties, planning, violence and democracy, hence the many 0 answers. Many answers on newer issues are low-confidence inferences.
